what: wave1b: does static YaRN repair retrieval past the native window? (64k and 128k, 3 depths).

protocol.why_these_lengths: Both test lengths exceed the model's native 32768 window, so the treatment has something to repair. wave1a (4k..32k) saturated and could not measure anything.
protocol.only_variable: rope scaling: base (shipped) vs yarn factor 4.0, original_max 32768

reading: YaRN removes the long-context failure entirely: base drops from 7/7 at 32k to 2/3 at 64k and 1/3 at 128k, yarn stays at 3/3. The failures are ordered, not scattered - base fails the needles FARTHEST from the question (depth 0.1 at 64k; depths 0.1 and 0.5 at 128k) and succeeds at depth 0.9, which sits nearest the end of the haystack and therefore nearest the query. That monotone-in-distance, monotone-in-length pattern is the signature of distance-based rotary extrapolation decay rather than sampling noise, which is what makes n=3 per cell informative here. It is still not an effect size: read it as 'the failure is real and YaRN removes it', not as 'YaRN is worth 67 points'.
caveats: n=3 per cell, deliberately spent on two long lengths rather than seven depths.
Both arms use --load-in-4bit, so the comparison is controlled; absolute base numbers would likely be higher in bf16, and quantization may amplify the gap.
Depths 0.25, 0.75 and 1.0 were not measured at these lengths - see the white cells in evidence/final_report/heatmaps.png.
Transport cross-check: the 12 rows were recovered twice by independent routes (NIAH_ROW lines in the kernel log, and the kernel output endpoint via sync_results) and agreed on every field.
